content: Myosin light chain kinase 2, also referred to as MYLK2, is an enzyme encoded by the MYLK2 gene in humans. This enzyme is a calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase that is specifically expressed in adult skeletal muscle tissue. The MYLK2 gene predominantly expresses skeletal muscle myosin light chain kinase (skMLCK) in fast-twitch muscle fibers, as opposed to slow-twitch muscle fibers. Calmodulin, a regulatory protein, consists of two terminal domains (N-terminal and C-terminal), each containing two EF-hand motifs that are capable of binding calcium ions (Ca2+). When calmodulin becomes saturated with calcium ions, it undergoes a conformational change. This structural alteration enables calmodulin to interact with target proteins, such as skMLCK. The binding of calmodulin to skMLCK enhances the enzyme's affinity for calcium ions, which ultimately facilitates sustained muscle contraction. Mutations in the MYLK2 gene have been associated with midventricular hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a condition characterized by abnormal thickening of the heart's midventricular walls.
